title: Bandwidth Abuse Detection
exclusions: Covers traffic through the web gateway only; byte counts are not available for requests the gateway blocks or does not decrypt. The CIM variant sums all categories because it does not filter by category.
evidence: Daily report export, kept for the acceptable-use review.

controlTest.positiveScenario: From a test user behind the web gateway, stream video from a site categorised as Video Sharing until more than 1 GB is transferred within the day. On the next daily run the user appears with `gb` above 1.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Have a second test user browse only business sites for the day. That user's requests are indexed but they do not appear in the results.

dataSources: `index=sse sourcetype=cisco:cloud_security:proxy` (or `cisco:umbrella:proxy` on older Umbrella exports) from the Secure Access or Umbrella S3 log bucket, read by the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569). One event per web request through the secure web gateway with `action`, `url`, `url_domain`, `category`, `blocked_category`, `user`, `identities`, `src_ip`, `bytes_in`, `bytes_out`, `http_method`, and `status`, tagged `web` and `proxy` for the CIM Web data model.
app: Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk ([Splunkbase 7569](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7569)), which reads Cisco Secure Access and Cisco Umbrella logs from the S3 log bucket and maps the web proxy log to the CIM Web data model. The companion Cisco Secure Access App (Splunkbase 5558) adds dashboards.
spl:
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:proxy", "cisco:umbrella:proxy")
| eval action=lower(action), total_bytes=coalesce(bytes_in, 0) + coalesce(bytes_out, 0)
| where action="allowed" AND match(category, "(?i)Video Sharing|Movies|Television|Music|Radio|Games|Social Networking|P2P")
| stats sum(total_bytes) as total_bytes values(category) as categories dc(url_domain) as domains by user
| where total_bytes > 1073741824
| eval gb=round(total_bytes/1073741824, 2)
| sort - gb
| table user gb domains categories
description: Totals bytes per user through the Secure Access or Umbrella web gateway to video sharing, movies, television, music, radio, games, social networking, and P2P file-sharing categories and lists users above 1 GB in the search window.
value: Heavy recreational streaming on a constrained branch or VPN link slows business applications for everyone on it. This report shows who is using the bandwidth and on what, so capacity and acceptable-use conversations start from data.
implementation: Collect the web proxy log with the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569) into `index=sse`. Run daily over 24 hours; adjust the 1 GB threshold to your link sizes.
visualization: Table: user, gb, domains, categories. Supporting panel: daily total bytes by category over 30 days (stacked area).
cimSpl:
| tstats summariesonly=true sum(Web.bytes) as total_bytes values(Web.category) as categories from datamodel=Web where Web.action="allowed" by Web.user
| rename Web.user as user
| where total_bytes > 1073741824
| eval gb=round(total_bytes/1073741824, 2)
| sort - gb
dataModelAcceleration: Enable acceleration on the CIM Web data model over `index=sse` before using the tstats variant.

Cisco Umbrella: Log Management and Amazon S3 log export

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Work video** — training platforms and video-conferencing replays may be categorised as Video Sharing. Add those domains to an exclusion lookup.

2. **Marketing and social media teams** — their job is on social platforms. Exclude their group or raise their threshold.

**Suppression:** a lookup of excluded domains and groups.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 7569) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Inputs Data Manager that reads the S3 bucket.
• Log export to Amazon S3 enabled in the Secure Access or Umbrella dashboard (Admin > Log Management), either a Cisco-managed bucket or your own, with the access key and secret for Splunk.
• An index for Secure Access and Umbrella data (this page uses `index=sse`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the network security team.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In the add-on create an S3 modular input for the web proxy log path with the bucket name, region, access key, and secret, and set the index to `sse`.
• Logs reach S3 in batches, so events usually arrive in Splunk 10 to 15 minutes after the request. `action` is logged as Allowed or Blocked (ALLOWED or BLOCKED in some exports); the searches lowercase it.
• Check the fields this search needs: run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:proxy" | stats count by action` over 1 day and confirm both values appear.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:proxy", "cisco:umbrella:proxy")
| eval action=lower(action), total_bytes=coalesce(bytes_in, 0) + coalesce(bytes_out, 0)
| where action="allowed" AND match(category, "(?i)Video Sharing|Movies|Television|Music|Radio|Games|Social Networking|P2P")
| stats sum(total_bytes) as total_bytes values(category) as categories dc(url_domain) as domains by user
| where total_bytes > 1073741824
| eval gb=round(total_bytes/1073741824, 2)
| sort - gb
| table user gb domains categories
```

Understanding this SPL
• `total_bytes` adds `bytes_in` and `bytes_out` with `coalesce` so a missing value counts as zero.
• The `match` keeps the Umbrella content categories that carry recreational media and file sharing; edit the list to your policy.
• `stats` per user totals bytes and lists categories and the number of domains, and the 1 GB threshold removes light users.

Accelerated variant over the CIM data model:
```spl
| tstats summariesonly=true sum(Web.bytes) as total_bytes values(Web.category) as categories from datamodel=Web where Web.action="allowed" by Web.user
| rename Web.user as user
| where total_bytes > 1073741824
| eval gb=round(total_bytes/1073741824, 2)
| sort - gb
```
• The tstats variant totals `Web.bytes` per user across all categories; add `Web.category` filters in the `where` clause if your CIM mapping carries the Secure Access category names.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Secure Access dashboard (or the Umbrella dashboard) under Reporting > Activity Search, filtered to Web and the same time range: the totals there should match the totals here within the S3 delivery delay.
• Pick the top user and confirm their traffic in Activity Search for the same day.
• Run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:proxy" | timechart span=1h count` over 7 days; gaps longer than an hour point to S3 input failures.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Run daily at 06:00 over the previous 24 hours and send to the network team.
• Use the 30-day panel in capacity planning for branch and VPN links.
• Raise repeated top users with their manager under the acceptable-use policy, not as a security incident.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No proxy events and S3 access errors (403 AccessDenied) in the add-on log: the access key cannot read the bucket or the region is wrong.
• Proxy events missing while DNS events arrive: the Secure Web Gateway is not enabled for those identities, or the S3 input path points at the DNS folder only.
• Events arrive hours late: the input polling interval is long, or the bucket path prefix is wrong and the input scans the whole bucket.
• `bytes_in` and `bytes_out` are empty: older Umbrella exports log `requestSize` and `responseSize`; map them with `eval` or update the add-on.
• The tstats variant returns nothing while the raw search works: the Web data model is not accelerated over `index=sse`, or the `cim_Web_indexes` macro does not include it.
grandmaExplanation: We find who uses the most internet for videos, games, and social media at work, so the network stays fast for everyone else.
